title: Level 5 (World Class) - A-1
notes:
West leads the ♠Q against 3NT. South has 4 tricks (the ♠A, ♠K, ♥A, and ♣A) outside of diamonds. South should try to take 5 diamond tricks. If diamonds are 3-2 there will be no problem.

Considering the diamond suit in isolation, South has a well known safety play available to guard against 4 diamonds to the ♦Q in East's hand. The safety play involves leading a low diamond from North towards the ♦J.

On this deal, it would be wrong to take this safety play. If South wins the spade lead in dummy to lead a low diamond towards the ♦J, East will play the ♦Q if he has it. South will have 5 diamond tricks, but the suit will be blocked. The defense will switch to hearts eventually knocking out dummy's side entry, the ♥A. South will go down if diamonds are 4-1.

South cannot guard against 4 diamonds to the ♦Q in East's hand. The only 4-1 diamond breaks South can guard against are singleton Queen with either West or East. South should win the ♠A in his hand and immediately duck a diamond.

The defenders can attack only 1 of dummy's entries. South can unblock the diamonds and dummy will still have an entry to get to the good diamonds.
